<!-- Generated by scripts/gen_opencode.py from .claude/commands/start.md. Edit the source, not this file. -->
In bash, run only one `python engine/<script>.py ...` command per call (never `python -c`, `Get-ChildItem`, `Get-Content`, `Test-Path` or pipes `|`); use the `read`, `glob`, `list`, `write` and `edit` tools for files.


Run the intake interview. It is resumable: `python engine/profile_cli.py intake` shows which stages are done. Start
at the first open stage (or the stage named in `$ARGUMENTS`). Ask one thing at a time. Keep their words.

0. `python engine/doctor.py --quick`, then `python engine/profile_cli.py init`, then `python engine/backup.py init`.

0b. **field.** Run `python engine/profile_cli.py packs` and ask which field they work in (show the names, not the ids).
   - A field with its own pack (for example software engineering): `profile_cli.py pack <id>`.
   - Any other field: `profile_cli.py pack general`. Then ask for the job titles they're after (two to six, in their
     words) and save them with `profile_cli.py titles "<title>, <title>"`.
   - Then, if the radar is empty, `python engine/radar.py seed` and say how many companies came with the pack (none
     for the general pack: `/radar add` builds the list).
   - `profile_cli.py intake done field`.

1. **documents.** Run `python engine/extract.py inbox`. Read each resume or document with
   `python engine/extract.py text inbox/<file>` (PDF, DOCX, TXT or EML). If a PDF comes out empty, it's a scan: open
   it with the file-reading tool instead. No documents? Ask them to drop their current resume into
   `inbox/`, or carry on from the interview alone. When a file has been read, move it with
   `python engine/extract.py archive inbox/<file>` and keep the printed archive path for the fact sources.
   Then `profile_cli.py intake done documents`.

2. **facts.** From the documents, draft facts: roles, responsibilities, achievements, metrics, tools, skills,
   certifications, education. Use one fact per claim, in their wording where it exists. Write them all as drafts in
   one payload: `python engine/facts.py add @data/tmp/facts.json`, each with `"source": "doc:<archive path>"`.
   Show them as a numbered table (id, kind, text, employer) in batches of about 10. They confirm, edit or delete:
   - `facts.py confirm f-0001,f-0002`;
   - `facts.py edit <id> @data/tmp/e.json --confirm` when they give new wording;
   - `facts.py retire <id> --note "<their reason>"`.

   Also write `profile/employment.json` and `education.json` with `profile_cli.py set employment|education
   @data/tmp/x.json`. Employers, titles and dates are exactly as they confirm them, `start`/`end` as YYYY-MM, `end`
   null for their current job. Then `intake done facts`.

3. **gaps.** Read `packs/<pack>/probes.json`: the `common` prompts, then those for their target families (analytics
   first). Ask only what the confirmed facts don't already answer.
   - Every answer that is a fact gets added and confirmed in the same turn, with `"source": "user"`.
   - A number they aren't sure of is stored as they said it (in `metrics[].as_said`), never rounded into a sharper
     claim.
   - "Don't know" is a valid answer and is recorded as such.
   - Anything that needs them to check something goes in `profile_cli.py intake ask "<question>"`.

   Stop when the probes are covered or they want to stop. Then `intake done gaps`.

4. **identity.** Collect their full name, the exact name form for resumes, email, phone, LinkedIn URL (optional) and
   current city and state. Save with `profile_cli.py set identity @data/tmp/id.json`. Then `intake done identity`.

5. **search rules.** Ask in this order, saying each default out loud. Record every answer verbatim with
   `profile_cli.py answer "<question>" "<their answer>"`.
   - Their current title and pay: `profile_cli.py current "<title>" --ctc <LPA> [--fixed <LPA>] [--variable <pct>]`.
     If the title isn't on the ladder, ask which level it equals and set `current.ladder_rank`.
   - Lower roles are never suggested. State this; it's a fixed rule, not a question.
   - How far up to look: "No limit on how senior, or drop roles more than N levels above yours?" (`rules.max_steps_up`,
     no limit by default).
   - Cities at home: "Any city in your country, or only certain ones (plus remote)?" Only on their explicit word, set
     `locations.home_cities_only`; say it's the one location rule that filters.
   - The lateral-move threshold: "A same-level move only if the pay rise is at least 20%. Keep 20%, or another
     number?" Then ask whether that's on total CTC or fixed pay.
   - Target families. Show the pack's families (`packs/<pack>/roles.json`) with the defaults ticked and the others
     unticked. They can add or remove any. Target titles (`profile_cli.py titles`) widen the search in any field.
   - Locations:
     - home country (India by default);
     - preferred cities or regions at home (a soft boost; say it never filters anything out);
     - places to avoid;
     - abroad: the countries they'd move to, in order of preference, and any cities in each. Add each with
       `profile_cli.py abroad add <country> [--cities "A, B"]`; every one counts as a country they can work in. Say
       the rule: abroad, only established companies, never a startup;
     - other countries they can work in but don't rank (rare);
     - pay or place: if pay matters more than where, set `locations.pay_over_place: true`;
     - remote yes or no, relocation yes or no.
   - Notice period in days (`notice_period_days`) and any deal-breakers.
   - Per-company limit: "Some people apply to at most N roles at one company at a time. Want a limit?" Only if they
     give one, save `rules.company_app_cap`; extra roles are then parked, still swept. No limit by default.
   - Applications they already sent before today: log each with `/applied ... --backfill` (no JD or resume needed).
   - Referrals: "I'll suggest at most 20 referral asks a day and one nudge after 5 days. Keep those?" Save as
     `referrals: {daily_cap, nudge_days}` in search.json.

   Save with `profile_cli.py set search @data/tmp/s.json`. Then `intake done search`.

6. **prefs.** Ask for PDF, DOCX or both, the page limit (default 2), and which contacts go on the resume. Save with
   `profile_cli.py set prefs @data/tmp/p.json`. Then `intake done prefs`.

7. **gmail (optional).** Ask: "Job-alert emails: paste them in (the default), or let the kit read them from a
   Gmail label every morning?" If they say paste, run `intake done gmail` and move on. If they want Gmail:
   - First `/radar recipes` (or `python engine/recipes.py`), so the alerts and the "Job Alerts" filter exist.
   - Then they double-click **Gmail setup.cmd** in this folder. It opens its own window, walks them through making a
     Gmail app password, and keeps it in Windows Credential Manager. Never ask them to type the password here, and
     never write it to a file.
   - When they say it's done, run `python engine/gmail_imap.py status`. Enabled: say so in one line. Not enabled:
     say what it reported and that paste-in stays. Then `intake done gmail`.

8. **close.** Show a summary table: facts (confirmed and draft counts), employers, the search rules, preferences and
   open questions. Run `python engine/backup.py commit "start: <stages done>"`. End with "Next: /radar".

Arguments for this command: $ARGUMENTS
